value.body: A warehouse executive makes sure goods come in, are stored and go out correctly and on time. Employers include e-commerce and retail firms, third-party logistics companies, manufacturers and distributors. A typical day involves supervising inbound and outbound work, checking stock in the warehouse system, and solving shortages, damages and delays.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BBA, B.Com or a degree with a supply-chain course

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Warehouse management systems, barcode scanners, Excel, ERP

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as warehouse, inventory or operations executives or trainees at logistics, e-commerce or retail firms. Comfort with shift work and spreadsheets helps; an internship at a fulfilment centre or warehouse is a common way in.

value.title: At a glance
items: The job is on-site and can involve night shifts and peak-season pressure.
Warehouses are often on city outskirts or in industrial areas.
Next roles: warehouse manager, inventory manager, or wider operations roles.
